info.name: SMemories - signatures (E11)
info.description:
Handwritten signatures on notes (T-095, epic E11, decision L-14): the optional `signature` part of `POST /api/public-collect/submit-note` (vector strokes, strict validation, re-serialised by the server), `data.signature` of `GET /api/public-collect/get`, and the `signature` of `GET /api/note/get-list` and `GET /api/book-data/get`. Run against an API started with SMEM_ENV=dev.

Accounts: the verified account A of postman/notes.postman_collection.json (`newman-notes-a@example.com`): run that collection's Setup once and `make verify-newman-users`. Run from the postman/ directory (`newman run signatures.postman_collection.json --working-dir .`) in order: Edge cases reuse the link and yearbook of the Full flow and end by deleting the yearbook. Each run creates its own yearbook, so it can run twice back to back.

The signature switch is per template (`"signature": true` in the manifest): `memory-book` and `navy-classic` declare it (T-097), `classic` and `modern` do not. The flow gives its yearbook the template in the variable `signatureTemplate` (default `memory-book`) and checks the round trip, canonical form, moderation and the validation table (`ERROR_INVALID_SIGNATURE`). At the end of Edge cases the book is switched to `classic`: the lookup says `enabled: false`, a valid signature is `ERROR_PARAM` and nothing is stored. An oversize (over 4 KiB) signature is `ERROR_INVALID_SIGNATURE` whatever the template: it is refused while the body is read, before the book (and so its template) is looked up.

item.name: Setup (once per database)
Register A (200; 409 or 429 when an earlier run already did)
Full flow
1. Login A
2. A creates a yearbook
2b. A picks the template named by the variable signatureTemplate (memory-book, which declares the signature switch) - 200
3. A creates a link
4. Public lookup: the form says whether the pad is offered, with the fixed limits

exec: pm.test('signature info', () => { pm.expect(Object.keys(s).sort()).to.eql(['enabled','h','max_points','max_strokes','w']); pm.expect([s.w, s.h, s.max_strokes, s.max_points]).to.eql([1000, 400, 12, 600]); });

item.name: 5. Friend signs (odd spacing and key order) - 200
6. Friend sends a note without a signature - 200
7. A reads the inbox: the signature is the canonical object, the note without one has null

exec:
const ints = (v) => Array.isArray(v) ? v.every(ints) : Number.isInteger(v);
const okSig = (s) => s === null || (Object.keys(s).join() === 'v,w,h,s' && s.v === 1 && s.w === 1000 && s.h === 400 && s.s.length >= 1 && s.s.length <= 12 && ints(s.s));
pm.test('every item has signature, integers only', () => items.forEach(i => { pm.expect(i).to.have.property('signature'); pm.expect(okSig(i.signature)).to.eql(true); }));
pm.test('the unsigned note has null', () => pm.expect(items.find(i => i.id === pm.collectionVariables.get('plainId')).signature).to.eql(null));
if (id) pm.test('the signed note comes back canonical', () => pm.expect(items.find(i => i.id === id).signature).to.eql({"v":1,"w":1000,"h":400,"s":[[120,260,300,120,480,280],[500,260,880,240]]}));

item.name: 8. A approves both notes - 200
9. Book data: the approved notes carry the signature (integers only), same shape for every note

exec:
const ints = (v) => Array.isArray(v) ? v.every(ints) : Number.isInteger(v);
const okSig = (s) => s === null || (Object.keys(s).join() === 'v,w,h,s' && s.v === 1 && s.w === 1000 && s.h === 400 && s.s.length >= 1 && s.s.length <= 12 && ints(s.s));
pm.test('every note has signature, integers only', () => notes.forEach(n => { pm.expect(n).to.have.property('signature'); pm.expect(okSig(n.signature)).to.eql(true); }));

item.name: 10. A hides both notes - 200
11. Book data after hiding: no notes, so no signature leaks

exec: pm.test('no stroke data in the body', () => pm.expect(pm.response.text()).to.not.include('"s":[['));
// Before every request of the flow: ', "<signedId>"' when the signed note exists, else nothing (the id list of the status calls).

item.name: Edge cases
Submit: duplicate signature part - 400 ERROR_PARAM
Submit: a signature over 4 KiB - 400 ERROR_INVALID_SIGNATURE
Submit: an empty signature part - 400 ERROR_INVALID_SIGNATURE

exec: pm.test('the rule is named, the content is not echoed', () => { const b = pm.response.json(); pm.expect(b.status).to.eql('ERROR_INVALID_SIGNATURE'); pm.expect(JSON.stringify(b)).to.not.include('SECRET'); });
